We look forward to your thoughts to advance towards an agreement beneficial for both parties.

Best regards.

edits.text: The Purchase Price shall be adjusted based on the Working Capital and Indebtedness of the Company as of the Closing Date, determined by reference to the Target Working Capital and Target Indebtedness set forth herein, with any excess or shortfall credited or debited accordingly.

For the avoidance of doubt, the initial purchase price of USD 45,000,000 is a base amount subject to upward or downward adjustment according to the agreed adjustment mechanism; no caps or floors shall apply to such adjustments.
The Buyer shall provide customary representations and warranties regarding the accuracy of the financial statements and related matters customary for a Buyer in a transaction of this nature.

The Closing shall occur within 30 days of signing; provided that the parties may mutually agree in writing to extend this period for an additional reasonable time to complete due diligence or satisfy closing conditions.

The confidentiality obligations of the parties shall be mutual, binding each party to maintain the confidentiality of the terms of this Agreement, subject to customary exceptions including disclosures required by law or to professional advisors.

We propose negotiating reasonable limits to protect our client's interests.

We also note the inclusion of Buyer representations regarding financial statements. We request that these be narrowly tailored to avoid undue exposure to liability on our side.

On the positive side, we welcome the mutual confidentiality provisions and the flexibility on closing timelines.

We look forward to your thoughts and a revised draft reflecting these points.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

probe.private_reasoning: The Seller initially proposed USD 45,000,000 as the purchase price with a clarification in the comment that this price excludes adjustments such as working capital and debt adjustments, which leaves room for upward or downward movements. In Round 2, the Seller added a detailed adjustment mechanism with no caps or floors, indicating flexibility in the final price depending on working capital and indebtedness. However, they have not indicated any willingness to reduce the base price below USD 45,000,000 intrinsically. Since no explicit reductions or concessions on base price were made and the Seller is asserting the initial price as a base subject to adjustment, I infer that 45 million USD is a hard floor on the actual price, and any downward adjustment would be limited to legitimate balance sheet criteria rather than negotiation concessions. Therefore, the lowest price the Seller will accept is very close to USD 45,000,000, potentially slightly less after adjustments but certainly not below 45 million as a starting point to negotiate from.
